name: Mobile car detailing
summary: Start a mobile car detailing business: your first 25 people and partners, a price menu by vehicle size from real ranges, quotes from the driveway and a maintenance plan that brings cars back.
door_hello: Your car, cleaned in your driveway
door_step3: I detail it in your driveway and send photos
door_rule: Hand these out in person or pin them on community boards. Never put flyers in or on a mailbox (18 U.S. Code 1725) or under windshield wipers where your city bans it.

promises.first_25: 15 people you know and 10 local dealers, repair shops and fleets, each with a message, plus flyers with the offer that fits the season.
promises.offer: Your price menu by vehicle size, the first-clients ladder, a maintenance plan and job math, on a one-page offer sheet.
promises.quote: Vehicle, package, condition and add-ons in; a quote, a text and an invoice out.
promises.keep: A thank-you, an honest review ask, your regular plan, a referral ask and a later check-in, each dated, plus review cards with your QR code.
promises.sample_one: A one-panel demo for one street or one partner business: a card to send, door hangers or a sample letter, and every message, saved to your Pipeline.
promises.reply: Paste what someone wrote back: what they meant, a short answer with one next step, and your Pipeline updated. A draft you send yourself.
promises.won: Log the yes, then everything for the detail: the booking text, a prep text, a printable job sheet, the after-job text and the invoice.
promises.proof: One car turned into proof: a result card, a before-and-after collage from your photos, a caption, an honest review ask and a case study once they say yes.
promises.next_25: The next 25 dealers, shops, fleets and agents near you that are not in your Pipeline yet, each with its messages, saved for Do my day.
promises.ready: Look ready before you reach out: a one-page website, a Google profile kit and a flyer, all from your real prices.
promises.fleets: Dealers, rental offices and trades with vans near you, each with a message, plus a per-vehicle rate sheet for an on-site wash day.

off_season.play: Sell interior-only details, holiday gift cards and monthly fleet washes while outdoor work is slow.

where_buyers_look.channel: Google Business Profile, Maps and reviews

sources.says: Your Google Business Profile is your strongest asset for getting found by local customers.

97% of consumers read reviews for local businesses; Google's share as a review source fell from 83% in 2025 to 71%; use of ChatGPT and other AI tools for local recommendations rose from 6% to 45%; 47% will not use a business with fewer than 20 reviews; 74% care about reviews from the last three months; 31% will only use a business with 4.5 stars or more and 68% with 4 or more; 80% are likely to use a business that responds to all of its reviews; 89% expect owners to respond.

licenses.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Rules differ by state, county and city: check your state and city.

items.what_to_check: Detailing is not a licensed trade in most states, but cities and counties usually require a business license.

sources.says: Licenses and permits depend on business activity and location; local governments set registration, licensing and permitting rules; research your own state, county and city; some licenses expire and must be renewed.
No license required in most states; you need a business license ($50 to $200), general liability and garage keepers coverage.

items.item: Garage keepers, general liability and commercial auto insurance
items.what_to_check: General liability does not cover damage to the customer's car while you work on it; garage keepers does. Commercial auto covers your work vehicle.

sources.says: Likely policies: general liability, commercial auto, garage keepers liability (crucial for detailers), tools and equipment insurance.

Lists common policies: general liability, product liability, professional liability, commercial property, home-based business insurance, and workers compensation; buy insurance required by law first, and taxes on employment insurance and workers compensation vary by state.

items.what_to_check: Do not let soapy water reach storm drains; use a water containment mat or rinseless methods where your city requires it. Ask the city stormwater office.

sources.says: Both commercial and residential vehicle wash water can contain contaminants (sediment, detergents, oils, grease, heavy metals); vehicle and equipment washing can add significant pollutants to stormwater if washwater is not properly captured and treated.
Regulations for mobile businesses vary by city or neighborhood; some areas have rules on water usage, runoff or operating a commercial service in a residential zone.

items.what_to_check: Apartment complexes, HOAs and office parks may ban commercial work or washing on site; get written permission before you set up.
items.note: judgment call, not a sourced fact

items.what_to_check: EIN is free from the IRS; some states tax car washing or detailing services, so ask your state revenue department.

sources.says: Get an EIN directly from the IRS online in minutes for free.

items.note: Sales tax treatment varies by state; not checked state by state.

steps: Booking: year, make, model and size; photos of the worst areas (pet hair, stains, odor); address; water and power access; any HOA or building rules; quote with each add-on as its own line.
Arrive and walk around the car with the customer; photograph existing scratches, dents and stains before touching anything.
Remove mats and trash; bag the customer's loose items.
Interior: blow out and vacuum, then extract or shampoo stains, clean dash, vents, trim and door jambs, condition leather, clean glass.
Exterior: wheels and tires first, pre-rinse or foam, hand wash with clean mitts, dry with microfiber, clay bar if booked, then wax or sealant, glass, tire dressing.
Contain wash water so it does not reach the storm drain.
Final walkthrough with the customer, after photos from the same angles, payment, review request, and book the next maintenance visit.

sources.says: Photograph the stained seat, trim damage and pet hair before starting; 68% of customers want photo, video or checklist proof of completed work (Housecall Pro 2025 Customer Service Report); break out upgrades as separate line items.
Mobile detailers often need space to work and may require access to water and electricity; confirm services and total cost in writing beforehand.

Both commercial and residential vehicle wash water can contain contaminants (sediment, detergents, oils, grease, heavy metals); vehicle and equipment washing can add significant pollutants to stormwater if washwater is not properly captured and treated.

job_checklist.note: Step order follows common detailing practice; a judgment call.

objections.objection: I found it cheaper online or at the car wash.
objections.answer: Ask what the other price included, then compare like for like (service level, vehicle size, time on site, products, mobile versus shop).

sources.says: When a customer finds a lower price: ask what they are comparing, then compare like for like; change the scope before the price.

objections.say: Could be a good deal! Let's compare like for like: what did theirs include, and how long were they on the car? I'm happy to change what's in mine to fit your budget instead of cutting corners.

objections.answer: Show the base price and each add-on as its own line, and the time it takes.

sources.says: A basic wash-and-vacuum takes 45 minutes; a full detail with pet hair, stains and engine bay can run three hours or more; break out upgrades as separate lines.

objections.say: Fair question. A full detail is a few hours of hand work, and every add-on is its own line on the quote, so you can drop anything you don't need. Want me to send it line by line?

objections.objection: Will you scratch my paint or ruin my seats?
objections.answer: Insured (garage keepers), before photos, the products you use, a redo promise.

sources.says: Common DIY mistakes include wrong chemicals that stain upholstery and buffers that create swirl marks; reputable mobile detailers are usually insured.

objections.say: I photograph the car before I start, I use clean microfiber and the right product for each surface, and I carry insurance through [your insurer]. If anything isn't right, tell me within 24 hours and I come back and fix it free.

objections.objection: Do you need my water and electricity?
objections.answer: Say exactly what you need, or bring a tank and generator for a fee.

sources.says: Mobile detailers may require access to water and electricity.

objections.say: I need an outdoor spigot and an outlet within reach of the car. If that's a problem where you park, tell me and we'll find a spot that has both.

objections.objection: I can just do it myself.
objections.answer: Fine for weekly washes; sell the deep work (extraction, correction, odor) and the time saved.

sources.says: DIY suits routine washes; hiring a pro is recommended for paint correction, deep shampooing and ceramic coating.

objections.say: Totally, regular washes are easy to do yourself. Where I help is the deep work: stains, pet hair, smells and paint that needs more than soap. Want a quote for just the inside?

objections.objection: Can you do it while I'm at work?
objections.answer: Yes if the lot owner allows it; get permission and a key handoff plan.
objections.note: judgment call, not a sourced fact
objections.say: Yes, if your building allows it. Check that a detailer can work in the lot, leave me the keys or a plan for them, and I'll text you photos when it's done.

seasonality.pattern: Spring peak (post-winter grime and people selling cars) and a second bump before winter for protection treatments.

sources.says: Detailing demand typically peaks in spring due to post-winter grime and pre-sale preparation, and again before winter as customers purchase protection treatments.

seasonality.pattern: Memberships and maintenance plans smooth out the slow months.
